svg.title: Six unpowered connections for the first distance sensor
svg.desc: Pi orientation with USB sockets at top and header at left. Physical pins 2,6,18,22. Breadboard resistor network with E at row3, M at row8, G at row14. Six connection table.
svg.text: Connect one distance sensor · six wires
Keep power unplugged. Read the sensor’s printed VCC / TRIG / ECHO / GND labels.
Components facing up · USB sockets at TOP
All four connections use the OUTER column.
Each horizontal group of FIVE holes is connected.
The centre gap separates the left and right groups.
Use the actual leg’s horizontal row;
resistor spacing can differ. Use LEFT-side holes.
3. Make these six connections while the Pi is unplugged
E, M and G are separate horizontal rows. M must join both resistors. G must join both ground wires.
ECHO goes through the first resistor to M. Never connect ECHO directly to a Pi GPIO.
With power unplugged, check each resistor leg and trace TRIG, ECHO and ground to the labelled pins.
Drawings show connection locations, not your exact lead shapes. Dashed lines are labels, not wires.
